_about: Permanent Court of International Justice (1922–1946), coded by hand from its published decisions (Series A, B and A/B on icj-cij.org). Each case groups the series entries that belong to it. Decision fields as in coding.json; refs are the PCIJ series numbers whose documents are linked. Advisory opinions carry a neutral description of the question unless the answer is well established.

cases.name: S.S. "Wimbledon" (United Kingdom, France, Italy and Japan v. Germany; Poland intervening)

decisions.s: Poland permitted to intervene.
Germany wrongly refused the Wimbledon passage through the Kiel Canal and must pay France 140,749.35 francs with interest at 6% from the judgment.

cases.name: Mavrommatis Palestine Concessions (Greece v. United Kingdom)

decisions.s: Jurisdiction upheld for the Jerusalem concessions, declined for those at Jaffa.
Mavrommatis's Jerusalem concessions were valid and the British authorities' conduct was not in conformity with Protocol XII, but no loss was proved and the claim for indemnity was dismissed.
No jurisdiction over Greece's later claim about readapting the concessions.

cases.name: Treaty of Neuilly, Article 179, Annex, Paragraph 4 (Bulgaria/Greece)

decisions.s: A chamber interpreted the treaty provision on Bulgarian liability for acts committed before Bulgaria entered the war.
Greece's request to interpret that judgment rejected.

cases.name: Certain German Interests in Polish Upper Silesia (Germany v. Poland)

decisions.s: Poland's preliminary objections rejected.
Poland's treatment of the Chorzów nitrate factory, and its notice to expropriate certain large estates, were not in conformity with the Geneva Convention on Upper Silesia.

cases.name: Denunciation of the Treaty of 2 November 1865 between China and Belgium (Belgium v. China)

decisions.s: The President indicated interim measures protecting Belgian nationals, property and shipping in China pending judgment; revoked on February 15, 1927 after the parties negotiated. The case was later removed from the list.

cases.name: Factory at Chorzów (Germany v. Poland)

decisions.s: Jurisdiction upheld over Germany's claim for reparation.
Germany's request for an interim payment on account refused, since it sought part of the final relief.
Interpretation of Judgments 7 and 8: the earlier finding on the Chorzów factory is binding on the parties.

Poland must pay compensation for the unlawful taking of the factory, measured by the value it would have had absent the wrong; reparation must wipe out the consequences of the illegal act. Expert inquiry ordered; the case was settled and withdrawn in 1929 before any sum was fixed.

cases.name: The S.S. "Lotus" (France v. Turkey)

decisions.s: By the President's casting vote, Turkey did not act contrary to international law in prosecuting the French officer of the Lotus after a collision on the high seas.

cases.name: Rights of Minorities in Upper Silesia (Minority Schools) (Germany v. Poland)

decisions.s: The Court interpreted the Upper Silesia Convention's rules on whether parents' declarations of a child's minority language could be verified or contested.

cases.name: Serbian Loans (France v. Kingdom of the Serbs, Croats and Slovenes)

decisions.s: The Serbian loans must be serviced in gold francs, as French bondholders claimed, not in depreciated paper francs.

cases.name: Brazilian Loans (France v. Brazil)

decisions.s: The Brazilian federal loans must be serviced on the basis of the gold franc.

cases.name: Territorial Jurisdiction of the International Commission of the River Oder (Germany, Czechoslovakia, Denmark, France, the United Kingdom and Sweden/Poland)

decisions.s: The Oder Commission's jurisdiction extends to the Warta and Noteć tributaries within Polish territory.

cases.name: Free Zones of Upper Savoy and the District of Gex (France/Switzerland)

decisions.s: The 1815 free zones remain in force, and France must withdraw its customs line from them by January 1, 1934.

cases.name: Interpretation of the Statute of the Memel Territory (United Kingdom, France, Italy and Japan v. Lithuania)

decisions.s: Lithuania's preliminary objection rejected.
The Governor of Memel could dismiss the President of the Directorate for serious acts, but some of the Lithuanian authorities' related steps were not in conformity with the Statute.

cases.name: Legal Status of the South-Eastern Territory of Greenland (Norway v. Denmark; Denmark v. Norway)

decisions.s: Norway's request for interim measures refused; the cases were withdrawn in 1933.

cases.name: Legal Status of Eastern Greenland (Denmark v. Norway)

decisions.s: Denmark held sovereignty over all of Greenland; Norway's 1931 declaration of occupation of Eastern Greenland was unlawful and invalid.

cases.name: Prince von Pless Administration (Germany v. Poland)

decisions.s: Germany's request for interim measures against tax enforcement treated as moot after Poland's undertakings; the case was later withdrawn.

cases.name: Polish Agrarian Reform and German Minority (Germany v. Poland)

decisions.s: Germany's request for interim measures refused as going beyond the subject of the case; the case was later withdrawn.

cases.name: Appeal from a Judgment of the Hungaro-Czechoslovak Mixed Arbitral Tribunal (The Peter Pázmány University) (Czechoslovakia v. Hungary)

decisions.s: Appeal rejected: Czechoslovakia must restore to the Peter Pázmány University the property it had taken over.

cases.name: Lighthouses Case between France and Greece

decisions.s: The 1913 Ottoman lighthouse concession held by a French firm was duly entered into and is operative against Greece.

cases.name: The Oscar Chinn Case (United Kingdom v. Belgium)

decisions.s: Belgium did not breach its obligations by its measures favoring a state-linked river transport company in the Congo.

cases.name: Pajzs, Csáky, Esterházy (Hungary v. Yugoslavia)

decisions.s: Hungary's appeal from the Mixed Arbitral Tribunal rejected; Yugoslavia's agrarian measures were not shown to breach the agreements.

cases.name: Diversion of Water from the Meuse (Netherlands v. Belgium)

decisions.s: The Netherlands' claims and Belgium's counter-claim both rejected.

cases.name: Lighthouses in Crete and Samos (France/Greece)

decisions.s: The lighthouse concession was operative as regards lighthouses in Crete and Samos.

cases.name: Borchgrave (Belgium v. Spain)

decisions.s: Spain's preliminary objections rejected; the case was withdrawn in 1938.

cases.name: Phosphates in Morocco (Italy v. France)

decisions.s: No jurisdiction: the dispute arose from facts before France accepted the Court's jurisdiction.

cases.name: Panevezys-Saldutiskis Railway (Estonia v. Lithuania)

decisions.s: Lithuania's objection upheld: local remedies had not been exhausted.

cases.name: Electricity Company of Sofia and Bulgaria (Belgium v. Bulgaria)

decisions.s: Bulgaria's objection partly upheld; the case proceeds on the rest.
Bulgaria must ensure that no step is taken capable of prejudicing the rights Belgium claims or aggravating the dispute; the war ended the case.

cases.name: Société Commerciale de Belgique (Belgium v. Greece)

decisions.s: Arbitral awards in the company's favor are binding on Greece; the Court declined to rule on how Greece should pay, given its financial position.

cases.name: Delimitation of the Territorial Waters between the Island of Castellorizo and the Coasts of Anatolia (Italy/Turkey)
Losinger (Switzerland v. Yugoslavia)
Designation of the Workers' Delegate for the Netherlands at the Third ILO Conference

decisions.s: The Netherlands' workers' delegate had been nominated in accordance with the Treaty of Versailles.

cases.name: Competence of the ILO in regard to Agricultural Labour

decisions.s: The ILO's competence extends to the conditions of persons employed in agriculture.

cases.name: Competence of the ILO to Examine Proposals on Methods of Agricultural Production

decisions.s: On whether the ILO could examine proposals for organizing agricultural production.

cases.name: Nationality Decrees Issued in Tunis and Morocco

decisions.s: The Franco-British dispute over the nationality decrees was not a matter solely within France's domestic jurisdiction.

cases.name: Status of Eastern Carelia

decisions.s: The Court declined to give an opinion, since Russia, a non-member party to the dispute, had not consented.

cases.name: German Settlers in Poland

decisions.s: Poland's measures evicting German settlers were not in conformity with its minority-protection obligations.

cases.name: Acquisition of Polish Nationality

decisions.s: On which persons acquired Polish nationality under the Minorities Treaty; the League Council was competent to address it.

cases.name: Jaworzina (Polish-Czechoslovakian Frontier)

decisions.s: The Conference of Ambassadors' 1920 decision had definitively settled the frontier in the Jaworzina district.

cases.name: Monastery of Saint-Naoum (Albanian Frontier)

decisions.s: The Conference of Ambassadors' allocation of the monastery to Albania was definitive.

cases.name: Exchange of Greek and Turkish Populations

decisions.s: On the meaning of "established" persons exempt from the Greek–Turkish population exchange.

cases.name: Polish Postal Service in Danzig

decisions.s: Poland's postal service in Danzig was not confined to its post office building.

cases.name: Interpretation of Article 3, Paragraph 2, of the Treaty of Lausanne (Mosul)

decisions.s: The League Council's decision on the Turkey–Iraq frontier would be binding, taken unanimously without the votes of the parties.

cases.name: Competence of the ILO to Regulate Incidentally the Personal Work of the Employer

decisions.s: The ILO could incidentally regulate employers' personal work when protecting workers.

cases.name: Jurisdiction of the European Commission of the Danube

decisions.s: On the Danube Commission's powers on the Galatz–Braila sector.

cases.name: Jurisdiction of the Courts of Danzig

decisions.s: Danzig railway officials could sue in Danzig courts on claims based on a Polish–Danzig agreement.

cases.name: Interpretation of the Greco-Turkish Agreement of 1 December 1926

decisions.s: On the mixed commission's power to refer questions to the arbitrator under the agreement.

cases.name: Greco-Bulgarian "Communities"

decisions.s: On the meaning of "community" in the Greco-Bulgarian emigration convention.

cases.name: Free City of Danzig and the ILO

decisions.s: Danzig's special status did not allow it to join the ILO without Poland's consent.

cases.name: Access to German Minority Schools in Upper Silesia

decisions.s: On whether children excluded after language tests could later be admitted to minority schools.

cases.name: Customs Regime between Germany and Austria

decisions.s: By eight votes to seven, the proposed Austro-German customs union was incompatible with Austria's 1922 Geneva Protocol.

cases.name: Railway Traffic between Lithuania and Poland

decisions.s: Lithuania was not obliged to open the Landwarów–Kaisiadorys railway sector to traffic.

cases.name: Access to, or Anchorage in, the Port of Danzig, of Polish War Vessels

decisions.s: The treaties gave Poland no general right of access for its warships to the port of Danzig.

cases.name: Treatment of Polish Nationals in the Danzig Territory

decisions.s: Poland could not invoke Danzig's constitution, only the treaties, about the treatment of its nationals there.

cases.name: Interpretation of the Greco-Bulgarian Agreement of 9 December 1927

decisions.s: On whether the Caphandaris–Molloff agreement obliged Greece to pay certain reparations sums.

cases.name: Interpretation of the 1919 Convention concerning Employment of Women during the Night

decisions.s: The convention applies to women in supervisory and managerial posts, not only manual workers.

cases.name: Minority Schools in Albania

decisions.s: Albania's abolition of private schools was not justified under its minorities declaration, which requires equality in fact as well as in law.

cases.name: Consistency of Certain Danzig Legislative Decrees with the Constitution of the Free City

decisions.s: Danzig's 1935 decrees letting judges punish acts by analogy to "sound popular feeling" were inconsistent with the Free City's constitution and the rule of law.
